Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:10:2.hebrew: לא קנאו - דמדעתיה אזל, ואין זו משיכה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:10:2.english: He has not acquired him - For he went of his own accord, and this is not pulling.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:11:1.hebrew: בשלמא לתנא דידן - לא תיקשי לשמואל אמאי לא תני משיכה במתניתין, דאיכא לתרוצי כדאוקמינן: דמילתא דאיתא במטלטלין לא קתני. אלא תנא ברא, דתנא חליפין בהדייהו, תיקשי לשמואל: אי איתיה דנקנה במשיכה, ליתנייה נמי במתניתין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:11:1.english: Granted, according to the tanna of our [mishna] - It is not difficult for Shmuel why [the tanna] does not teach pulling in our mishna, for it can be answered as we established: that a matter that applies to movable property, he does not teach. But [according to] the external tanna, who taught [symbolic] exchange alongside them, it is difficult for Shmuel: If it is [indeed] so that [a slave] is acquired through pulling, let him teach it as well in his teaching.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:11:2.hebrew: מילתא דאיתא בין במקרקעי בין במטלטלי - כגון חליפין — צירף ושנה עם השאר דאיתנהו במקרקעי; אבל משיכה, דליתא במקרקעי — לא תנא בהדייהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:11:2.english: A matter that applies both to land and to movable property - Such as symbolic exchange — he combined and taught [it] along with the rest that apply to land. But pulling, which does not apply to land, he did not teach along with them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:12:1.hebrew: כיצד במסירה - גבי בהמה קאי, דקתני מתני' (לקמן קידושין דף כה:): בהמה גסה נקנית במסירה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:12:1.english: How [is it done] through passing - [This] refers to an animal, as the mishna teaches (below, Kiddushin 25b): "A large animal is acquired through passing."

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:12:2.english: By its hair - For example, the hair on the head of a horse.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:14:1.hebrew: אדעתא דמרה אזלא - על דעת הקורא אותה, לפי שאין לה דעת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:14:1.english: [It] walks by the will of its owner - By the will of the one who calls it, because it has no mind [of its own].

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:14:2.english: Of his own will - Of his own volition:

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:14:3.hebrew: קטן - דלית ליה דעת, כבהמה דמי. ואם קראו לשם קניה ובא אצלו — קנאו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:14:3.english: A minor - Since he has no understanding, he is considered like an animal. And if he called him for the sake of acquisition and he came to him, he has acquired him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:15:1.english: [If] he untied his shoe - The slave [did so] for the purchaser.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:15:2.hebrew: גרדו - גראט"ר (גרטי"ר: לגרד) בלע"ז:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:15:2.english: Scraped him - *Grater* (*gratier*: to scrape), in Old French.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:15:3.english: He lifted him - The slave [lifted] the purchaser.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:15:4.hebrew: מאי קאמר - מה ענין הגבהה דעלמא להגבהה דהכא? הגבהה דעלמא — לוקח מגביה החפץ, והכא אמרינן שהעבד מגביהו, משום עבודה שהלוקח משעבד בו לקנותו בחזקה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:15:4.english: What is [Rabbi Shimon] saying - What does ordinary lifting have to do with the lifting here? [In] ordinary lifting, the buyer lifts the object, whereas here, we say that the slave lifts him [the master], as a service that the buyer subjects him to in order to acquire him through possession.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:17:1.hebrew: אלא מעתה - דהגביהו הוא לרבו, קנאו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:17:1.english: If that is so - That [if the slave] lifted his master, [the master] acquires him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:17:2.english: A Canaanite maidservant should be acquired through intercourse - For behold, he lifts her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:19:1.hebrew: הנדואה - מארץ כושי. כוש מתרגמינן הינדואה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:19:1.english: From India [Hindo’ah] - [He was] from the land of Cush; [the name] “Cush” is translated [in the Targum as] “Hindo’ah.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:19:2.english: That the world was overpowering him - [He was] moribund and nearing death.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:19:3.english: He said to him - Mar Zutra [said] to the slave of the convert.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:19:4.hebrew: שלוף לי מסנאי - לקנותו בחזקה היה מתכוון, שיהא בעבודתו כשימות אדונו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:19:4.english: Remove my shoes - He intended to acquire him through an act of possession [chazakah], so that he would be [engaged] in his service when his master dies.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:19:5.hebrew: איכא דאמרי גדול היה - העבד, ונזהר בו שלא יזכה הוא עצמו מן ההפקר. לפיכך קדם לפני המיתה וזכה בו, והגר פירש למיתה ומר זוטרא פירש לחיים תחתיו, שלא יהא העבד בלא אדון רגע אחד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:19:5.english: There are those who say he was an adult - The slave [was an adult], and [Mar Zutra] was careful regarding him lest he acquire himself from ownerless property. Therefore, he acted before [the convert's] death and acquired him; and [thus] the convert departed to death and Mar Zutra departed to life in his stead, so that the slave would not be without a master for even a single moment.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:1:1.english: Had it been stated: “And you shall put his ear to the door,” I would say: He should pierce opposite his ear into the door - But he would not pierce the ear.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:2:1.hebrew: לאזן מאבראי - כלומר, רחוק מן הדלת, כדכתיב: "את אזנו" — והדר יתן אזנו בדלת, ויקח את המרצע וידקור בדלת מעבר השני כנגד אזנו, לקיים: "ולקחת המרצע ונתת באזנו בדלת":
Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:2:1.english: The ear outside - That is to say, far from the door, as it is written: “[...shall pierce] his ear”; and then he places his ear against the door, and takes the awl and pierces the door from the other side opposite his ear, in order to fulfill: “And you shall take the awl and put it through his ear and into the door.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:2:2.hebrew: דוקר ויורד - אזנו כשנותנה על הדלת, עד שמגיע לדלת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:2:2.english: He pierces and goes down - [Through] his ear when he places it on the door, until he reaches the door.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:3:1.english: Detached - From the doorpost and lying on the ground.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:3:2.english: Just as a doorpost is upright - For otherwise, it is not called a doorpost.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:4:1.english: A bundle - A bundle of pearls and a bundle of spices hung around the neck as an ornament.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:6:1.english: And he acquires himself - From his master.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:6:2.hebrew: בכסף ע"י אחרים - שיתנוהו לרבו ע"מ שיהא זה בן חורין, אבל הוא עצמו לא יקבל מהם, ואפילו ע"מ שאין לרבו רשות בו, דקסבר: אין קנין לעבד בלא רבו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:6:2.english: By money through others - That they give it to his master on condition that this [slave] will be a free man; but he himself may not receive [the money] from them, even on condition that his master has no rights to it, for he holds [that] a slave has no acquisition without his master.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:6:3.hebrew: ובשטר ע"י עצמו - שיקבלנו הוא. ובגמרא מפרש לכולה דרבי מאיר ורבנן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:6:3.english: And by a bill [of manumission] through himself - That he himself receives it. And in the Gemara, it explains the entirety of [the dispute between] Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:6:4.hebrew: ובלבד שיהא הכסף משל אחרים - דעבד אין לו כלום, דאם מצא מציאה או קבל מתנה — הכל לרבו. ואם בא לפדות ע"י עצמו, צריך להיות משל אחרים, ויתנוהו לו ע"מ שאין לרבו רשות בו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:6:4.english: Provided that the money belongs to others - For a slave possesses nothing, as if he found a lost article or received a gift, it all belongs to his master. And if he comes to redeem [himself] by himself, [the money] must belong to others, and they must give it to him on condition that his master has no right to it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:7:1.hebrew: שדה נקנית בכל הני - ולקמן יליף בפירקין (דף כו.). וכל עובדי כוכבים ככנענים משנמכר לעבד; אלא שכל עבדים נקראין על שם כנען, משום דכתיב ביה (בראשית ט): ״עבד עבדים״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:7:1.english: A field is acquired through all these - And later in our chapter (26a), [the Gemara] derives [this]. And all idolaters are like Canaanites once [one is] sold as a slave; rather, all slaves are called by the name of Canaan because it is written concerning him (Genesis 9): “A slave of slaves.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:9:1.hebrew: מילתא - דאיתיה בעבד וליתא בשאר מטלטלין קתני. אבל חליפין, דאיתנהו נמי בשאר מטלטלין — שהמטלטלין גם הם נקנין בחליפין — לא איצטריך ליה למיתני:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22b:9:1.english: A matter - [That] which applies to a slave and does not apply to other movable property, he teaches. But symbolic exchange, which also applies to other movable property — as movable property is also acquired through symbolic exchange — he did not need to teach.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 22b:19:1.hebrew: איכא דאמרי גדול היה - העבד, ונזהר בו שלא יזכה הוא בעצמו מן ההפקר; לפיכך קדם לפני המיתה וזכה בו. "זה פירש למיתה" — יהודה הינדואה, "וזה פירש לחיים" — מר זוטרא, תחתיו במקומו, שלא יהיה העבד רגע אחד בלא אדון:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 22b:19:1.english: "There are those who say he was an adult" - [Namely,] the slave. And [Mar Zutra] was careful regarding him, lest he [the slave] acquire himself from the ownerless property; therefore, he acted before the death and acquired him. "This one departed to death" — [this is] Yehuda from India; "and this one departed to life" — [this is] Mar Zutra, [stepping in] in his stead, in his place, so that the slave would not be for even a single moment without a master.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 22b:4:1.hebrew: כמין חומר - פירש הקונטרס: צרור מרגליות או בשמים, שתלוי בצואר נשים לתכשיט. ור"ת פירש: חומר — מעשה. וכן פירש הערוך: בלשון ערבי, כשאומר לחבירו "מה מעשיך", אומר לו "מה חמרך":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 22b:4:1.english: “As a type of ḥomer” - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: A bundle of pearls or spices that hangs on women’s necks as an ornament. And Rabbeinu Tam explained: Ḥomer [means] an action. And so explained the Arukh: In the Arabic language, when one says to his fellow, “What are your deeds?”, he says to him, “What is your ḥamr?”

Tosafot on Kiddushin 22b:4:2.hebrew: מה נשתנה אזן - יש במדרש דמרצ"ע בגימטריא ד' מאות (שנה); ולפי שהיו ישראל עבדים ארבע מאות שנה וגאלם הקב"ה, והלך זה וקנה אדון לעצמו — לפיכך ירצע במרצע העולה כך:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 22b:4:2.english: "Why is the ear different" - There is [a teaching] in the Midrash that [the word] martzea [awl] is in gematria four hundred (years); and since Israel were slaves for four hundred years and the Holy One, Blessed be He, redeemed them, and this [man] went and acquired a master for himself — therefore, let him be pierced with an awl, which amounts to this [number].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 22b:8:1.hebrew: [ת"ל לעולם כו' - ואין לומר לעולמו של יובל, דא"כ לשתוק קרא מיניה ונילף משדה אחוזה. ת"י]:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 22b:8:1.english: ["The verse states: 'Forever…'"] - And one cannot say [that "forever" means] the "forever" of the Jubilee, for if so, let Scripture be silent about it and let us derive [it] from an ancestral field. — [Tosafot Yeshanim]
